                          EASTPORT PORT AUTHORITY, MAINE

                                  MOTION TO INTERVENE

       Pursuant to Rule 214 of the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission’s (“FERC”) Rules of

Practice and Procedure, the Eastport Port Authority (“Port Authority”), by and through its

undersigned counsel, Rudman Winchell, moves to intervene in the above-referenced proceeding

regarding the DeepGreen Western Passage SPV LLC (“DeepGreen”) preliminary permit

application for the proposed Subsea-Compute and Infrastructure Hub Project (“Project”). 18

C.F.R. § 385.214. By this motion, the Port Authority seeks to ensure that their interests are

adequately represented during FERC’s evaluation of the Project. In support of its motion, the

Port Authority states the following:

                                  CONTACT INFORMATION

       Pursuant to Rule 2010 of the Commission’s Rules of Practice and Procedure, 18 C.F.R. §

385.2010, all filings, orders, and correspondence regarding this proceeding should be served as

follows:

                               DESCRIPTION OF INTERVENOR

        The Eastport Port Authority was created by act of Maine State Legislature in 1977. P. &

S.L. 1977, Ch. 14. The Port Authority has the authority to acquire, construct, operate, maintain,

repair and replace piers, terminal and warehouse facilities on the land and in the waters within

the limits of the City of Eastport. Id.

                                   THE PROPOSED PROJECT

        On February 11, 2026, and supplemented and amended on June 8, 2026, and July 30,

2026, DeepGreen filed an application pursuant to Section 4(f) of the Federal Power Act (FPA)

for a preliminary permit in order to study the feasibility of the proposed underwater data center

Project. If approved, the Project would be located in the Western Passage of the Bay of Fundy in

the North Atlantic Ocean in and adjacent to the waters of the City of Eastport, Washington

County, Maine. On August 25, 2026, FERC published Notice of this Project in the Federal

Register and set deadlines for filing comments, motions to intervene, competing applications

(without notices of intent), or notices of intent to file competing applications.

        The proposed Project would consist of the following new features: (1) a 3.5-meter-high

and 24-meter-wide subsea modular universal docking cradle; (2) thirty-four 12-meter-long and

4.2-meter-diameter subsea compute pods; (3) a 1.8-meter-diameter spherical and elevated tidal

sensing power platform; (4) up to 16 marine hydrokinetic turbine-generator units, each rated at

                                                                                                    2
 300-kilowatt (kW); and (5) a 1.5-mile-long hybrid power-and-fiber subsea cable operating at

13.8 kilovolts (kV). The proposed Project would be configured as a behind-the-meter captive

generation loop without a grid connection. The Project would be situated in the Western Passage

of the Bay of Fundy. The Project would include a single, armored 1.5-mile hybrid power-and-

fiber subsea cable, which lands at a shore-based facility on Kendall Head. The Project boundary

would be restricted to 27.1 acres.

                       THE PORT AUTHORITY HAS AN INTEREST

                          IN THE OUTCOME OF THE PROCEEDING

        The Port Authority states the following in compliance with Rule 214(b) of the

Commission’s Rules of Practice and Procedure, 18 C.F.R. § 385.214(b):

i. 18 C.F.R. § 385.214(b)(1) Position of Movant:

        The Port Authority opposes the Project. The Port Authority further reserves the right to

supplement this position based on additional anticipated submissions by DeepGreen or other

interested parties.

ii. 18 C.F.R. § 385.214(b)(2) Right to Participate and Representation of an Interest Affected

by the Proceeding:

        The Port Authority has a right to seek intervention to become a party as conferred in 18

C.F.R. § 385.214(a)(3).

        In this proceeding, DeepGreen proposes a hybrid tidal-energy/data-center facility in the

Western Passage of the Bay of Fundy. The Project location includes and is adjacent to the waters

within the limits of the City of Eastport, where the Port Authority has the authority to acquire,

construct, operate, maintain, repair and replace piers, terminal and warehouse facilities. The

proposed Project may impact the Port Authority’s infrastructure. Therefore, the Port Authority



                                                                                                    3
 has a direct and substantial interest in this proceeding that cannot adequately be represented by

any other party. Additionally, the siting and the construction of the proposed Project would have

the potential to significantly affect the citizens and businesses that rely on the Port Authority’s

infrastructure. Therefore, the Port Authority seeks to intervene to ensure it receives sufficient

notice and is afforded the opportunity to comment, as necessary, as more details about the Project

become available.

                                          CONCLUSION

       The Port Authority has a substantial interest in this proceeding due to the fact that the

Project is proposed to be located within and adjacent to waters the Port Authority has the

authority to acquire, construct, operate, maintain, repair and replace piers, terminal and

warehouse facilities. The Port Authority respectfully requests that the Commission grant the Port

Authority’s Motion to Intervene in the DeepGreen Western Passage Subsea-Compute &

Infrastructure Hub Project No. 15424-000.
